docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Agent pods / inference pods: tools · models · serving engines
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Kubernetes: kubelet · CRI · Cilium networking and policy
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
OuterSpace Core: Linux · systemd · containerd · optional Dragonfly
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Qualified CPU UEFI virtual machines: AMD64 / ARM64

The Agent and Inference profiles share one build and maintenance stream. Each shipped image has its own manifest, source/image identity, SBOM and qualification records. A passing result for one profile never promotes another image. The Kubernetes control plane, Cilium and application workloads are deployed separately from the host image.

docs.title: Image layout
docs.text:
Partition Purpose Alpha status EFI system partition systemd-boot and unified kernel image UEFI boot qualified; Secure Boot disabled OOS_ROOT Read-only ext4 host filesystem dm-verity data OOS_VERITY Root hash tree Expected hash embedded in UKI OOS_STATE Persistent /var Runtime images, rotated kubelet identity and bounded logs; unencrypted

The current image has one root slot. dm-verity detects root-filesystem corruption; it does not provide authenticated boot by itself. Signed boot, authenticated A/B updates and rollback remain future qualification work. The running host does not use in-place apt upgrades.

docs.title: Native execution and networking
docs.text:
containerd uses overlayfs, systemd cgroups and CRI. Kubelet has anonymous authentication disabled, webhook authorization, TLS bootstrap and certificate rotation. The actual CPU candidates have passed enrollment, Cilium/Envoy readiness, DNS/service traffic, default-deny/allow checks and cold-boot recovery.

The Agent v1 profile combines native admission, AppArmor, seccomp and cgroup v2 limits. It qualifies a shared-kernel OCI workload within one trusted administrative domain. Revocable workload authority, external approval brokers, fleet quarantine and VM-backed tenant isolation remain distinct roadmap items.

Inference qualifies a separately pinned CPU serving workload. Model containers and weights have their own provenance and licenses; they are not part of the OS image's redistribution approval.

docs.title: OCI delivery and persistent state
docs.text:
Dragonfly is enabled through explicit node configuration. Containerd retains HTTPS origin resolution and content-digest verification. Kubelet owns runtime image garbage collection, with a 24-hour maximum unused age and 80%/65% pressure thresholds. Dragonfly's peer cache has a separate six-hour TTL.

End-to-end P2P, private-registry authorization, peer security and fleet cache lifecycle remain unqualified. Model-weight caching is a separate lifecycle. No throughput or storage-reduction guarantee is implied by the architecture.

See the architecture decisions and worker configuration.

docs.title: What is available now?
docs.text: 0.1.0-alpha.1 has four qualified CPU images: Agent and Inference on AMD64 and ARM64. The first milestone is complete and the release is prepared as a draft. Public downloads will appear on GitHub Releases after publication. There is no stable release.

docs.title: Is this a container image?
docs.text: It is an operating-system disk image for Kubernetes workers. Containers hold the Agent or Inference workloads. Both profiles share one immutable Core, but each shipped image is qualified separately.

docs.title: Does the alpha run a real model?
docs.text: Yes. The Inference candidates passed a separately pinned CPU serving workload, including replacement, drain and recovery after node restart. The model weights and serving container are not bundled into the host or covered by its licenses.

docs.title: Does an attestation enable Secure Boot?
docs.text: No. The GitHub attestation authenticates the checksum inventory and its build provenance. Secure Boot and authenticated A/B updates have separate, unfinished gates. The alpha uses UEFI with Secure Boot disabled.

docs.title: Is GPU or bare-metal operation supported?
docs.text: Neither has a qualified hardware matrix yet. Evaluate this alpha in disposable UEFI VMs. Driver/kernel/CDI integration and physical hardware tests are later work.

docs.title: Does Dragonfly eliminate local image storage?
docs.text: Each node still needs the image layers it executes. Optional peer delivery can share OCI content, while model-weight storage remains separate. P2P, private registry authorization and fleet cache lifecycle are not yet qualified.

docs.title: Is it production ready or CIS certified?
docs.text: No. This is an experimental CPU alpha with explicit limits and release gates. In particular, the time-limited kernel risk acceptance excludes host VPNs and custom networking.

docs.title: Is it a Flatcar fork?
docs.text: No. OuterSpace maintains its own Ubuntu-based image and source-built kernel/runtime inputs, with independently packaged Agent and Inference profiles.

docs.title: Capabilities and status
docs.text:
Execution foundation is complete: seven delivery issues closed. The four CPU candidates for 0.1.0-alpha.1 passed independently. The release is currently a draft.

Area Qualified or implemented in this alpha Remaining scope Worker profiles Independent Agent/Inference images on AMD64 and ARM64 Bare-metal and GPU hardware matrices Boot and state Two UEFI boots, read-only dm-verity root, persistent state Authenticated Secure Boot and A/B rollback Kubernetes Real OuterSpace nodes, CRI, certificate rotation and cold-boot recovery Fleet-scale lifecycle and upgrades Networking Cilium/Envoy, DNS/services and default-deny/allow on each image Custom networking and host VPNs Agent execution Native OCI admission, AppArmor/seccomp enforcement and resource-pressure cases Scoped credentials, approvals, egress mediation and quarantine Inference Real CPU model serving, replacement, drain and recovery GPU/CDI, shared tenancy and serving QoS Resource evidence Static baselines and trusted operation-phase measurements Hardware capacity claims and adaptive-budget research OCI delivery Optional native Dragonfly component and explicit routing P2P, private auth, peer security and cache lifecycle qualification Supply chain SBOMs, sources/notices, reviewed vulnerabilities and attested checksums Ongoing updates and renewal of expiring decisions Release Four qualified CPU candidates and verified draft preparation Public publication, then later beta/RC/stable gates

The roadmap tracks the remaining Agent security and Fleet qualification milestones. No general latency, energy, image-size reduction or CIS compliance claim follows from these reference results. See security and release information.

docs.title: Build and evaluate the CPU alpha
docs.text: The 0.1.0-alpha.1 images are qualified and prepared as a draft. Published downloads will appear on GitHub Releases. Read the alpha limitations before evaluating a worker.

docs.title: Build from source
docs.text:
Install Python 3.11+, Make and Docker running Linux containers. The build uses Docker's native architecture: ARM64 on Apple Silicon, AMD64 on x86 hosts. Allow space for image output, source archives and reusable download caches.

git clone https://github.com/Alien6-Studio/outerspace-os.git
cd outerspace-os
git checkout v0.1.0-alpha.1
make check
make PROFILE=agent HARDWARE=cpu builder build smoke package
# Build the other profile independently:
make PROFILE=inference HARDWARE=cpu build smoke package

Images, bundles and reports are written under out/<profile>-cpu-<architecture>/; .cache/ holds reusable downloads. The builder uses privileged Linux mount namespaces without a host Docker socket or host devices mounted inside it.

The smoke test boots the packaged image through UEFI twice and checks persistence, read-only root, verity, cgroup v2/PSI, kernel BPF/BTF, AppArmor, CRI availability and host resource budgets. Native enrollment and workload qualification are separate targets; make help lists them.

docs.title: Verify and boot a downloaded candidate
docs.text:
Check the archive checksum, then extract the distribution bundle into a new directory. The accompanying .tar.attestation.jsonl authenticates its inner SHA256SUMS, not the outer tar file. Use the release's verify-attestation.py companion with the expected commit, tag and candidate run from the release notes. Then run sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS inside the bundle before using the disk image.

Use a disposable UEFI VM with four vCPUs and 4 GiB RAM, with Secure Boot disabled. The qualified configuration uses a separate Kubernetes 1.36 control plane and Cilium 1.20.3 with the supplied src/cluster/cilium configuration. This worker image does not create the control plane.

docs.title: Configure a worker
docs.text:
From the corresponding source checkout, supply the real cluster CA, a protected short-lived bootstrap-token file and the HTTPS API address:

python3 build/tools/node-config.py \
  --api-server https://api.example.net:6443 \
  --ca /secure/cluster-ca.crt \
  --token-file /secure/bootstrap-token \
  --cluster-dns 10.96.0.10
make config-drive

Attach out/node-config.raw only to the intended worker. It contains credentials; keep it private, detach it after enrollment and revoke the bootstrap token. The worker retains its rotated identity in persistent state. Use an explicit control-plane policy for serving-certificate CSR approval.

See the worker guide for the Agent profile, CPU serving and native qualification commands. The outerspace and root accounts are locked; the image provides no SSH server or shared password.

docs.title: One OS, two worker profiles
docs.text:
OuterSpace OS is an Ubuntu-based Linux distribution for Kubernetes workers. The shared Core supplies the kernel, systemd, containerd, kubelet and immutable node identity. Agent frameworks, inference engines, models and their language libraries run in separately deployed containers.

Version 0.1.0-alpha.1 is qualified for CPU evaluation and prepared as a draft. The first milestone, Execution foundation, is complete. Public downloads await publication of the draft; there is no stable or supported production release.

docs.title: Qualified today
docs.text:
• Agent: native OCI admission and isolation, enforced resource limits, pressure scenarios and recovery after worker restart.
  • Inference: real CPU model serving, workload replacement and drain/recovery.
  • Both: separate AMD64 and ARM64 images, UEFI boot, Kubernetes/Cilium enrollment, certificate rotation and cold-boot recovery on the actual OuterSpace kernel.

The host combines Ubuntu 24.04 LTS packages with source-built Linux 6.18.60 and pinned runtimes. A read-only dm-verity root is paired with persistent /var. Dragonfly is an optional OCI delivery component; its fleet/P2P qualification is still separate work.

docs.title: Evaluation scope
docs.text:
Use disposable UEFI VMs and a separate, self-managed Kubernetes control plane. The native qualification used four vCPUs and 4 GiB RAM per worker. Bare-metal, GPU, authenticated updates and production support have not been qualified. Host VPNs and custom network configurations are outside the alpha's reviewed scope.

Start with build and test, architecture and the alpha release information.

docs.title: Releases and maintenance
docs.text: Current version: 0.1.0-alpha.1 — qualified CPU alpha, release in draft. Execution foundation is closed with all seven delivery issues completed. The draft contains the four qualified images and their verification material. Public downloads will appear on GitHub Releases after publication; no stable or production release is claimed.

docs.title: What the first alpha qualifies
docs.text:
Profile Architectures Native scenarios Agent AMD64, ARM64 OCI admission/isolation, resource-pressure cases and worker recovery Inference AMD64, ARM64 Real CPU serving, workload replacement/drain and worker recovery

All four images passed two UEFI boots, persistence and host budgets, Kubernetes/Cilium enrollment, certificate rotation, cold-boot recovery and their own security/redistribution gates. Integration records also retain the static Agent resource and operation-phase baselines with their exact image identities.

The distributions include checksums, GitHub attestations, SBOMs, 2,554 corresponding-source objects and 120 original APT notices per reviewed inventory. The release also preserves the native and integration records and provides a verification companion. Attestations authenticate the inner SHA256SUMS; they are not Secure Boot signatures.

  • Qualified version source
  • Four-candidate qualification
  • Verified draft preparation
  • Remaining roadmap

docs.title: Evaluation limits
docs.text:
Use disposable CPU UEFI VMs; the native reference setup has four vCPUs and 4 GiB RAM with Secure Boot disabled. A separate Kubernetes control plane is required. Bare-metal/GPU qualification, authenticated A/B updates, production support and performance guarantees are not included. Persistent state is unencrypted.

The accepted CVE-2019-14899 risk expires on 14 November 2026 at 06:24:43 UTC and applies only to the stock CPU configuration without host VPNs or custom networking. No universal kernel fix is claimed. Model weights and application containers have separate provenance and licensing requirements.

docs.title: Qualification phases
docs.text:
OuterSpace uses its own MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH version, independent of Ubuntu, Linux and Kubernetes. A version tag alone does not establish support.

Phase Intended use Required evidence Alpha Explicit experimental preview Boot, CRI, configuration, checksums, notes, licenses/sources, SBOM, vulnerability review and profile-specific workload gates Beta Integration testing Alpha gates plus cluster readiness, Cilium, P2P, image GC and state persistence Release candidate Hardware/security qualification Beta gates plus bare metal, CIS audit, signed boot and upgrade/rollback Stable Supported operation within a published matrix RC gates plus soak evidence and an explicit support policy

The policy and release process are authoritative. Release CI prepares a draft from existing qualified artifacts; promotion does not rebuild them. Publication and later stages remain explicit decisions.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text: Update reviewed, pinned inputs and deploy whole images. Preserve the source, profile, architecture and image identity with every result. Reassess expiring vulnerability decisions and retain original upstream notices. No supported in-place update path or production support window is offered by this alpha.

docs.title: Security scope
docs.text:
The CPU alpha has passed actual-image boot, native workload and supply-chain checks. The Agent profile has demonstrated admission refusals, AppArmor/seccomp enforcement, bounded resource pressure and recovery. These results qualify the stated shared-kernel profile, not arbitrary untrusted tenancy or production use.

Each distribution includes an SBOM, corresponding sources, original notices, unfiltered vulnerability reports and accountable review decisions. The four checksum inventories have GitHub attestations tied to their exact source, tag and candidate workflow. Promotion verifies every payload before preparing a draft.

docs.title: Time-limited accepted risk
docs.text:
CVE-2019-14899 is accepted only for the stock CPU alpha until 14 November 2026, 06:24:43 UTC. No host VPN client or configured VPN tunnel is included in this qualification. IPsec/XFRM remains compiled for Cilium; no universal kernel fix is claimed. Host VPN setup and custom network configurations are outside this scope.

The recorded kernel non-applicability decisions and source/notice reviews are conditional on the verified inputs and configuration. Unknown findings remain blocking, and expired decisions must be reviewed again.

docs.title: Remaining limits
docs.text:
• UKIs are unsigned; dm-verity alone does not authenticate boot. Disable Secure Boot for this alpha.
  • Persistent state is unencrypted, and no authenticated A/B updater or rollback is supplied.
  • Bare-metal and GPU configurations have not been qualified.
  • Agent authority brokers, fleet quarantine, private P2P authorization and peer security remain roadmap work.
  • A full CIS audit and production support commitment are not present.

CIS Ubuntu Level 1 Server remains an audit target with explicit Kubernetes/eBPF tailoring, not a certification. Hardware, signed updates and fleet adversarial qualification belong to the later milestones.

See the security policy and recorded release decisions. Report vulnerabilities through the repository's private advisory channel.

docs.title: OuterSpace OS by Alien6
docs.text:
OuterSpace OS is a distribution project by Alien6, focused on a small, purpose-built host for Kubernetes inference workers.

The visual identity retains its original planetary illustration and pink/violet palette. The faceted orbital mark and ASCII boot banner connect the website with the operating system. The footer follows the same “by Alien6” attribution used by Trunx, Signal and Ruleflow.

Development happens in the GitHub repository. The distribution source lives on main; website source and generated pages live on gh-pages. Original OuterSpace source is licensed under Apache-2.0. Ubuntu packages and bundled upstream components retain their own licenses.
